risks.note: Management flags fluctuations in demand due to global economic conditions or geopolitical factors; the business is tied to construction and infrastructure cycles.

The rapid pace of technological change necessitates continual innovation to stay competitive, in an industry management itself describes as moving to energy-efficient, smart and connected, automated elevator systems.
Potential disruptions in the supply chain, especially for critical components in electronics and semiconductors, which would affect manufacturing and project execution.
Increasing reliance on digital systems poses significant cybersecurity risks that management says need to be managed.
Listed among threats as intense competition in the technology solutions market, requiring constant innovation and adaptation.

risks.risk: Geopolitical risk to global supply chains
risks.note: Flagged as a threat, particularly in the semiconductor and defense sectors, which would feed through to imported components.
Flagged as a threat: economic uncertainties that may lead to reduced spending on R&D and technology upgrades.

Management ties financial performance to timely execution of projects, quality control and customer service, and to execution of existing orders, so results depend on the order book converting on schedule.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: L. T. Elevator Limited is a Kolkata-headquartered SME-listed manufacturer of passenger, goods, home and hospital elevators that also installs, commissions and maintains them, with 351 permanent employees as on 31 March 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is primarily engaged in manufacturing, producing, assembling, purchasing, selling, importing, exporting and stocking all kinds of elevators, including their spares, accessories and allied components, and also acts as trader, commission agent, broker, distributor, dealer and marketing agent for elevators and their spares and accessories. Its key products and services span manufacturing, installation, commissioning and annual maintenance of passenger elevators, goods/car elevators, home elevators and hospital elevators for high-rise, residential, commercial, hospitality, healthcare and infrastructure projects. Automated multi-level car parking solutions are offered through its subsidiary, Park Smart Solutions Limited.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Park Smart Solutions Limited — subsidiary: Sole subsidiary listed in Form AOC-1 Part A; incorporated January 11, 2019; reporting period and reporting currency both stated as NA (same as the holding company). Also named in Form AOC-2 (as Park Smart Solution Limited) as a related party for investment and purchase transactions entered into in the ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis.
- Nishit Gupta — related party: Relative of a Director; transaction nature is remuneration, entered into in the ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis.
- Arvind Gupta — related party: Managing Director; transaction nature is remuneration, unsecured loan from Director and unsecured loan repayment to Director, on an arm's length basis.
- Usha Gupta — related party: Whole-time Director; transaction nature is remuneration, on an arm's length basis.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Elevators: 55% of order book; B2C (D2C) growing rapidly — 35% of revenue targeted in FY27 (from negligible in FY26); B2G: 30-35% in FY27; B2B: ~30%; Car Parking: 45% of order book; government projects include Shillong Smart City (INR13cr completed in FY26, INR30cr in FY27), plus two other INR33cr and INR43cr projects under execution

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Elevators and vertical transportation systems:** Passenger elevators, Goods/car elevators, Home elevators, Hospital elevators, Elevator spares, accessories and allied components, Installation, commissioning and annual maintenance services
- **Car parking (through subsidiary Park Smart Solutions Limited):** Automated multi-level car parking solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- High-rise buildings
- Residential complexes
- Shopping malls
- Hospitals
- Hotels
- Commercial and industrial projects
- Infrastructure and smart-city projects

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR250cr (LT+Park Smart); Ricardo separately: INR70-80cr (not consolidated); split: 55% elevators, 45% car parking

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: >80% YoY in FY27; margin: sustain 25% EBITDA; order inflow: targeting 100+ B2C elevators/month; capex/commissioning: INR25cr total for new plant, commissioning by March 2027 (Q4FY27)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: D2C brand scaling across 21 Indian offices; exports to Malaysia, Australia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia; new 6.5-acre plant enables 2.5x capacity to INR350-400cr; potential car parking acquisitions under exploration

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Steady elevator-industry growth driven by rapid urbanization, infrastructure development, increasing construction activities and the expansion of residential, commercial and industrial projects
- Rising demand for elevators, spares and accessories from high-rise buildings, shopping malls, hospitals, hotels, residential complexes and other infrastructure projects
- Industry adoption of modern technologies: energy-efficient elevators, smart and connected systems, advanced safety features and automated solutions
- Increasing emphasis on passenger safety, convenience, energy efficiency and modernization of existing elevator systems, expected to create further opportunities for manufacturers, traders, distributors, dealers and service providers
- Smart city initiatives and construction of residential and commercial projects cited as significant opportunities for the elevator and vertical transportation industry
- Growing demand for automated and multi-level car parking solutions, described as an additional growth opportunity through the subsidiary
- Management states the outlook for the coming year remains positive with expected growth across both business verticals; the same Opportunities and Outlook paragraph, however, anticipates strong demand in the aerospace, defense and telecom sectors and benefits to the power systems market from renewable energy and smart grid infrastructure, which is inconsistent with the elevator business described everywhere else in the report and reads as boilerplate text
- The Company aims to leverage its manufacturing capabilities, technical expertise and established market presence to expand its customer base and order book (no order-book value disclosed)
- The Company remains focused on improving operational efficiency, strengthening its order book and achieving sustainable growth in the coming years
- Financial performance is stated to have been supported by execution of existing orders and continued business development

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: B2B/B2G gross margin ~50%; D2C gross margin 58-60%; EBITDA margin sustainable at 25%; raw material (steel) cost pressure mitigated by April 2026 price hikes and escalation clauses in govt contracts

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Merger with Ricardo Elevators (low single-digit dilution); capex for new plant; funding working capital via D2C’s advance payments (50-55% upfront); no dividend or buyback mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no named capex or expansion project, no commissioning or ramp timeline and no rupee quantum. Expansion is described only in intent: the Company aims to leverage its manufacturing capabilities, technical expertise and established market presence to expand its customer base and order book, and states it remains focused on expanding its operations and delivering safe, reliable and energy-efficient solutions. The only identified new-growth avenue is the automated and multi-level car parking opportunity pursued through the subsidiary Park Smart Solutions Limited. Manufacturing and project sites are referred to generically in the EHS paragraph, but no plant location, capacity or capacity addition is disclosed.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly bullish, confident, and execution-focused; emphasized ‘starting line’ of growth; transparent on bottlenecks and proactive on solutions; no hedging on raw materials but pricing power demonstrated

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Manufacturing capabilities the Company states it aims to leverage to expand its customer base and order book
- Technical expertise and an established market presence in the elevator and vertical transportation industry
- Integrated offering spanning manufacturing, installation, commissioning and annual maintenance, which supports recurring service revenue from the installed base
- Adjacent exposure to automated and multi-level car parking demand through the subsidiary Park Smart Solutions Limited
- Internal control systems stated to be reviewed periodically by the audit committee for adequacy and effectiveness

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delayed govt payments (4-month cycle); integration risk of Ricardo (though execution already consolidated); steel price volatility; execution pressure from INR300cr+ order book before new plant is live

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: D2C elevators have 58-60% gross margin — higher than industry norms due to customization and brand premium; exports priced 50% above India with no white-labeling; Ricardo’s order book is already being executed by LT — merger is administrative, not operational; 21 offices enable 400-500km coverage, making logistics feasible without heavy inventory

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Leverage manufacturing capabilities, technical expertise and established market presence to expand the customer base and order book
- Maintain operational focus on timely execution of projects, quality control and customer service
- Improve operational efficiency, strengthen the order book and achieve sustainable growth in the coming years
- Expand operations while delivering safe, reliable and energy-efficient solutions
- Pursue growth in automated and multi-level car parking solutions through the subsidiary Park Smart Solutions Limited
- Strengthen the financial position and generate sustainable …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Regulation 30 intimation of a proposed acquisition of Dongyang PC, Inc. (Seoul, Korea; est. 2002), a specialized manufacturer of mechanical parking systems, via a signed and executed Share Purchase Agreement; upon completion DYPC becomes a subsidiary and is expected to become wholly owned (100%) after the buyback step.
- [DYPC IP & scale] DYPC holds 12 registered patents (plus 4 additional patent applications pending) and 21 registered trademarks, 2 registered design rights, has supplied 739+ parking units across 35 countries via a 10+ country distribution network, and its SMART PARKING® brand is registered in 18 countries.
- [Flagship references] Notable DYPC installations cited: Intel Corporation, Israel (13 units, 208 parking spaces, high-spec commercial); Enso Village, California USA (10 units, ASCE 7 certified, high-seismic zone, 108 spaces); Devonshire, Singapore (72 cars, 2x AC36 towers, prime residential).
